In perfumery it brings a classic white floral elegance to fresh bouquets. In India, lily's clean beauty suits daytime and festive occasions. In summer, its fresh purity is welcome. Timeless white floral grace.
honeysuckle: Honeysuckle smells sweet, honeyed and nectar-rich with climbing-vine lushness and sunny warmth. The flower's sweet scent is beloved in gardens. In perfumery it brings a sweet, sunny floralcy to spring and summer compositions. In India, honeysuckle's sweet warmth suits pleasant weather. In summer heat it can cloy, so enjoy in moderation. Nectar-sweet floral joy.
african-orange-flower: African orange flower refers to orange blossom from North Africa, particularly Morocco and Tunisia, with exceptional radiance and honeyed depth. In perfumery it represents premium orange blossom quality. In Indian summers, its luminous character is glorious. The finest orange blossom tradition.
narcissus: Narcissus, including daffodil and jonquil, smells green, hay-like and hypnotically floral with a distinctive animalic undertone. The spring bulb's scent is complex and slightly narcotic. In perfumery it adds a sophisticated green-floral depth to chypres and niche compositions. In India, its spring character suits the brief cool season. Complex spring beauty.
white-flowers: White flowers is a blended impression of jasmine, tuberose, orange blossom and their kin, all creamy white petals and heady sweetness. In perfumery it signals lush, romantic white floral abundance. In India, white flower bouquets are beloved for evenings and celebrations. In summer nights they bloom magnificently. In daytime heat, choose lighter interpretations. White floral opulence.
frangipani: Frangipani, or plumeria, smells creamy, tropical and sweetly floral with coconut-like warmth, the flower of Hawaiian leis and Balinese temples. In India, where it is called champa, frangipani is beloved. In perfumery it brings exotic tropical creaminess to summer compositions. In Indian summers, frangipani's tropical nature thrives. In winter it feels like a holiday memory. Pure tropical bliss.
tiare-flower: Tiare flower is the Tahitian gardenia, smelling creamy, tropical and intensely sweet with monoi-oil richness. It is the flower of the South Pacific. In perfumery it defines tropical white florals. In India, tiare's exotic creaminess suits summer holidays and beach moods. The essence of tropical paradise.
egyptian-jasmine: Egyptian jasmine grows in the Nile Delta, producing flowers of exceptional richness and indolic depth. In perfumery, Egyptian origin signals premium jasmine quality. In Indian summers, its powerful nocturnal character blooms dramatically. The jasmine of pharaohs.
hedione: Hedione is the molecule that gives jasmine its radiant, airy lift, smelling fresh, transparent and subtly floral-citrus with an almost effervescent quality. It does not smell like jasmine itself but makes everything smell more luminous. In perfumery it is in countless fresh florals. In India, hedione's airy radiance is perfect for summer, adding lightness. Invisible radiance in molecular form.
indian-jasmine: Indian jasmine, the mogra and chameli of subcontinental nights, smells intensely sweet, indolic and narcotic with unparalleled tropical richness. India's jasmine is legendary, garlanding gods, brides and festivals. In perfumery, Indian jasmine absolute represents the pinnacle of jasmine intensity. In Indian summers, its powerful bloom is transcendent. The soul of Indian nights in flower form.
lemon-blossom: Lemon blossom smells fresh, citrusy-floral and delicately sweet with the bright promise of fruit to come. In perfumery it brings a sparkling citrus-floral lightness to fresh compositions. In India, its bright freshness suits summer days. Citrus groves in bloom.
white-lily: White lily is lily at its purest, all pristine white petals, green freshness and elegant sweetness. In perfumery it represents the cleanest white floral expression. In India, white lily's pure beauty suits formal occasions and daytime elegance. In summer, its clean freshness is welcome. Purity in flower form.
indian-tuberose: Indian tuberose, the rajnigandha that perfumes Indian nights, is more intense and narcotic than its Western counterparts, with unparalleled creamy power. In perfumery, Indian origin marks the most potent tuberose. In Indian summers, its nocturnal majesty is legendary. Handle with respect, this flower does not whisper.
water-jasmine: Water jasmine is a delicate, aquatic interpretation of jasmine, sheer and translucent with watery freshness. In perfumery it offers jasmine's beauty in a light, summer-friendly form. In Indian summers, water jasmine's sheer freshness is ideal, all the romance without the weight. Jasmine for hot days.
vanilla-flower: Vanilla flower is the delicate orchid bloom before it becomes the spice, smelling soft, creamy-floral with subtle vanilla warmth. In perfumery it offers vanilla's gentle floral side. In India, its soft creaminess suits refined tastes. Vanilla's innocent youth.
tunisian-orange-blossom: Tunisian orange blossom, from the Cap Bon peninsula, is considered the world's finest, with exceptional radiance and honeyed complexity. In perfumery it marks luxury white floral compositions. In Indian summers, its luminous perfection is unmatched. The pinnacle of orange blossom.
night-blooming-jasmine: Night-blooming jasmine, though botanically distinct, shares jasmine's nocturnal intensity, releasing powerful sweet fragrance after dark. In India, night-blooming flowers define the sensory experience of summer evenings. In perfumery it inspires the most intoxicating nocturnal white florals. In Indian summers, its after-dark power is magical. Mystery that blooms at midnight.
sandalwood: Sandalwood, particularly Mysore sandalwood, is India's gift to world perfumery, creamy, soft, warm and meditatively smooth with unparalleled elegance. The now-rare Mysore variety was legendary. In perfumery, sandalwood is the ultimate creamy wood, essential to orientals and meditative compositions. In India, chandan carries spiritual significance, used in worship and Ayurveda for millennia. In all weather, sandalwood's creamy calm soothes. In summer it stays smooth; in winter it glows. The most beloved wood in perfumery.
patchouli: Patchouli smells earthy, dark and richly woody with chocolate-like depth and hippie-era associations, though fine patchouli is far more refined. Aged patchouli develops incredible smoothness. In perfumery it anchors chypres, orientals and bohemian compositions. In India, patchouli's earthy richness suits winter and monsoon. In summer, it can feel heavy, so choose lighter doses. From head-shop to haute parfumerie, patchouli endures.
cedar: Cedar smells dry, woody and pencil-shaving crisp with clean, aromatic warmth. In perfumery it is the workhorse wood, providing structure to countless masculine and fresh-woody compositions. In India, cedar's dry cleanliness works well in summer, cutting through humidity. In winter, it adds crisp structure. Reliable, clean wood.
vetiver: Vetiver, or khus, is deeply Indian, its roots woven into cooling screens (tattis) that scent summer air. The oil smells earthy, green, smoky and complex with remarkable depth. In perfumery vetiver defines an entire family of elegant earthy scents. In Indian summers, vetiver is a revelation, its earthy coolness is the scent of monsoon relief. In winter, its smoky depth warms. India's fragrant root, beloved worldwide.
agarwood-(oud): Agarwood, the source of oud, forms when Aquilaria trees fight infection, creating dark, resinous wood of extraordinary complexity. It smells animalic, woody, sweet and profoundly deep. In India and the Middle East, oud is the pinnacle of perfumery, worth more than gold. In perfumery it defines luxury oriental compositions. In Indian winters, oud's magnificent depth unfolds over hours. In summer, use the lightest touches. The king of woods.
woody-notes: Woody notes is a general term for the dry, warm, structural character of woods in perfumery, the backbone of masculine and elegant compositions. In perfumery it indicates warm, natural depth. In India, woody scents are versatile year-round, with lighter woods for summer and richer ones for winter. The foundation of perfumery.
virginia-cedar: Virginia cedar, or red cedar, smells warm, sweet-woody and slightly smoky with a distinctive pencil-shaving character. In perfumery it is a staple of masculine woody compositions. In India, its warm dryness suits cooler months. Classic American wood.
woodsy-notes: Woodsy notes evokes the general impression of forests and woods, natural, earthy and grounding. In perfumery it suggests an outdoorsy, natural character. In India, woodsy scents connect with nature escapes. In pleasant weather, they are comforting. Forest air in a bottle.
guaiac-wood: Guaiac wood smells smoky, sweet and rosy-woody with a distinctive barbecue-like warmth and incense character. From South American trees, it brings an exotic smokiness to perfumery. In perfumery it enriches woody orientals with sweet smoke. In Indian winters, guaiac's sweet smokiness is captivating. Exotic smoked wood.
cashmere-wood: Cashmere wood is a soft, musky-woody synthetic smelling like blonde woods, soft skin and cosy warmth. It creates the cashmere-sweater effect in modern perfumery. In perfumery it is ubiquitous in soft woody-musky compositions. In India, its soft warmth suits winter and air-conditioned offices year-round. Comfort in wood form.
cypress: Cypress smells green-woody, dry and Mediterranean with distinctive aromatic freshness and cemetery solemnity. In perfumery it brings a dry, elegant greenness to chypres and Mediterranean compositions. In India, cypress's dry elegance offers contrast to tropical lushness. In pleasant weather, it is refined. Mediterranean dignity.
cashmeran: Cashmeran is the molecule behind cashmere wood's soft, musky-woody warmth with a distinctive spicy-pineapple nuance. In perfumery it creates the modern soft-wood signature. In India, its cosy character suits winter and offices. The molecule of modern comfort.
juniper: Juniper smells green, piney and gin-like with crisp, aromatic freshness and berry sweetness. In perfumery it brings a bracing, botanical freshness to aromatic and fresh compositions. In India, juniper's crisp greenness is refreshing in summer. In winter, it adds festive brightness. The botanical behind gin.
juniper-berries: Juniper berries are the piney, sweet-tart fruits behind gin, smelling crisp, green and aromatically fresh. In perfumery they add a bright, botanical sparkle to fresh compositions. In India, their crisp freshness suits summer. Botanical brightness.
amberwood: Amberwood is a synthetic woody-amber molecule smelling dry, warm and modern with a distinctive cedar-amber character. It defines many contemporary masculine fragrances. In perfumery it provides a modern woody backbone. In India, its dry warmth works year-round, performing well in heat. The sound of modern masculinity.
cypriol-oil-or-nagarmotha: Cypriol, or nagarmotha, is an Indian root smelling earthy, woody and smoky with distinctive papyrus-like dryness. Used in Ayurveda and Indian perfumery for centuries. In perfumery it adds an authentic Indian earthy-smoky depth to orientals. In India, nagarmotha's native character resonates deeply. In winter and monsoon, its earthy depth shines. India's smoky root treasure.
haitian-vetiver: Haitian vetiver is prized for its clean, green, slightly nutty character, less smoky than Indian varieties. In perfumery it represents refined, elegant vetiver. In Indian summers, its clean greenness is beautifully refreshing. Vetiver at its most polished.
brazilian-rosewood: Brazilian rosewood smells rich, rosy-woody and sweet with luxurious depth, now protected and rare. In vintage perfumery it was treasured. In modern scents it is mostly a memory. In India, its legendary status intrigues collectors. A ghost of perfumery's past.
palisander-rosewood: Palisander rosewood is the romantic French name for Brazilian rosewood, the legendary timber that defined luxury perfumery in the early 20th century. It smells rich, rosy-woody and warmly sweet with a distinctive floral-wood character unlike any other timber. True Brazilian rosewood is now protected under CITES regulations, making it a ghost ingredient, present in vintage masterpieces but rarely in modern scents. In perfumery, its name evokes an era of opulence, ocean liners, grand hotels and unapologetic luxury. Modern palisander accords attempt to capture its rosy warmth with sustainable materials. In India, its vintage charm appeals to collectors and connoisseurs who appreciate perfumery heritage. In winter, palisander-type warmth is wonderfully nostalgic. A beautiful echo of a lost golden age.
white-woods: White woods is a blended impression of light, clean woods, cedar, blonde woods and soft musks, all airy transparency. In perfumery it creates modern, minimalist woody freshness. In India, white woods' clean lightness is perfect for summer and offices. Woody minimalism.
atlas-cedar: Atlas cedar grows in Morocco's Atlas Mountains, producing wood oil of exceptional quality, warm, sweet and honeyed with a distinctive richness that sets it apart from other cedars. The high-altitude terroir creates a more complex, almost amber-like cedar. In fine perfumery, Atlas origin marks premium woody compositions. In India, Atlas cedar's warm richness shines in winter, when its honeyed depth unfolds beautifully in cool air. It elevates any woody composition it touches. For cedar lovers seeking the finest expression, Atlas is the connoisseur's choice. Mountain-grown luxury.
papyrus: Papyrus smells dry, earthy and ancient, like old paper and desert reeds with distinctive arid warmth. In perfumery it adds a dry, intellectual earthiness to niche compositions. In India, its arid character offers contrast. Ancient paper and desert winds.
oak: Oak in perfumery brings the robust, tannic warmth of the mighty tree, all woody strength, subtle vanilla from the grain and natural authority. It smells like whisky barrels, old libraries and forest cathedrals. In perfumery, oak adds a solid, masculine woodiness to leather, tobacco and oriental compositions, giving them backbone and gravitas. In India, oak's sturdy character suits confident wearers and formal occasions. In winter, its warm strength is reassuring and powerful. It pairs beautifully with leather and smoke for the ultimate distinguished character. Strength, tradition and quiet power in wood form.
balsam-fir: Balsam fir smells like Christmas, resinous, green and sweetly coniferous with festive warmth. In perfumery it brings a joyful, resinous greenness to winter compositions. In India, its festive character suits the holiday season. Christmas tree in a bottle.
vetyver: Vetyver is simply the French spelling of vetiver, the beloved earthy root, and in perfumery the French spelling often signals classic French vetiver compositions in the tradition of Guerlain and Givenchy. The scent is identical, earthy, green, smoky and elegantly complex. In India, where vetiver is khus with deep cultural roots, the French spelling adds a touch of Parisian chic to a deeply Indian ingredient. In all weather, vetyver's timeless elegance endures. In summer, its earthy coolness refreshes; in winter, its smoky depth warms. The same beloved root, with French polish.
teak-wood: Teak wood smells rich, warm and oily-smooth with distinctive tropical hardwood depth. In perfumery it brings a luxurious tropical woodiness. In India, where teak is treasured, this note feels like home. In winter, teak's rich warmth glows. Tropical hardwood luxury.
driftwood: Driftwood captures the poetic scent of timber weathered by ocean, sun and time, all salty smoothness, bleached warmth and marine-woody character. It smells like beachcombing, like wood made silky by waves and pale by sun. In perfumery, driftwood accords blend salty marine notes with dry woods and soft musks to create a sense of coastal calm and natural weathering. They appear in niche marine-woody compositions and minimalist beach-inspired scents. In India, with its vast coastline, driftwood scents resonate beautifully, they smell like Goa's beaches, Andaman shores and lazy coastal holidays. In summer, their salty-woody freshness is perfect for beach days and coastal evenings. In winter, they offer a nostalgic escape to warmer shores. Ocean-smoothed tranquility.
indonesian-patchouli-leaf: Indonesian patchouli leaf produces oil of exceptional quality, dark, rich and chocolatey with superior depth. Indonesia is now the primary source. In perfumery it represents patchouli at its finest. In Indian winters, its rich earthiness is magnificent. Patchouli perfected.
precious-woods: Precious woods is a blended impression of rare, luxurious woods, sandalwood, rosewood, oud, all warmth and opulence. In perfumery it signals luxury woody richness. In India, precious woods' opulence suits winter celebrations. Liquid luxury in wood form.
amyris: Amyris, or West Indian sandalwood, smells creamy, woody and sweet with sandalwood-like softness at a fraction of the cost. In perfumery it provides an affordable creamy wood. In India, its gentle creaminess is versatile. Sandalwood's accessible cousin.
pine: Pine smells resinous, green and sharply fresh with mountain-forest clarity and turpentine brightness. In perfumery it brings a bracing coniferous freshness to fresh and winter compositions. In India, pine evokes Himalayan forests. In winter, its crisp freshness is invigorating. Mountain air in scent form.
pine-tree: Pine tree emphasises the whole tree experience, needles, bark and resin in natural harmony. In perfumery it creates authentic forest impressions. In India, pine forests are a beloved escape. In winter, pine scents transport you to the mountains. The whole forest.
white-cedar-extract: White cedar extract offers a refined, pale interpretation of cedarwood, cleaner and softer than standard cedar with elegant woody transparency. It provides woody structure without heaviness. In perfumery, it is prized for modern, minimalist woody compositions where clarity matters. In India, white cedar's clean lightness is ideal for summer and office wear, giving woody sophistication without overwhelming in heat. It layers beautifully under other notes. Cedar distilled to its most elegant essence.
fir: Fir smells green, balsamic and resinously fresh with Christmas-tree character and forest depth. In perfumery it brings natural coniferous freshness. In India, fir evokes mountain escapes. In winter, its festive greenness delights. Forest freshness.
mahogany: Mahogany smells rich, warm and polished with a distinctive reddish-brown woodiness and luxurious depth. It evokes gentlemen's clubs, polished boardrooms and vintage luxury, all dark wood panelling and leather chairs. In perfumery, mahogany brings an opulent, warm woodiness to distinguished oriental and woody compositions. In Indian winters, mahogany's rich warmth is perfect for formal evenings and special occasions, projecting success and sophistication. It blends beautifully with tobacco, cognac and amber for the ultimate power scent. For those who want their fragrance to smell like achievement. Luxury in timber form.
australian-sandalwood: Australian sandalwood is the sustainable alternative to Mysore, creamy and warm though slightly less complex. In perfumery it provides ethical creamy wood. In India, it offers sandalwood comfort with a clear conscience. Creamy wood, responsibly sourced.
smoke: Smoke in perfumery smells of incense, bonfires and smouldering woods, mysterious and primal with endless depth. In perfumery it defines an entire aesthetic of fire and mystery. In Indian winters, smoky scents are transcendent around bonfires. In summer, use the sheerest touches. Primal and captivating.
cedarwood: Cedarwood is the essential oil of cedar, dry, clean and aromatically woody with classic pencil-shaving character. In perfumery it is fundamental to woody compositions. In India, its dry cleanliness cuts through humidity. The essential wood.
virginian-cedar: Virginian cedar, also called red cedar, is the classic American cedarwood oil, warm, sweet-woody and dry with the familiar pencil-shaving character beloved in traditional masculine perfumery. It has been a staple woody material for over a century. In perfumery, Virginian cedar provides reliable, clean woody structure to fougeres, chypres and woody orientals. In India, its dry cleanliness works well in summer, cutting through humidity with crisp woodiness. In winter, it adds warm structure to richer compositions. It may lack the romance of rarer woods, but its honest, dependable character has earned its place. The workhorse of woody perfumery.
white-wood: White wood is a soft, clean woody impression, light and modern with musky transparency. In perfumery it creates airy woody freshness. In India, white wood's lightness is ideal for summer. Wood at its lightest.
iso-e-super: Iso E Super is the molecule behind a velvety, woody-violet warmth with a distinctive radiant, almost pheromone-like quality. It is in countless modern fragrances. In perfumery it creates the contemporary woody signature. In India, its smooth warmth works year-round. The molecule of modern perfumery.
oud: Oud, from infected agarwood trees, is perfumery's most precious material, animalic, woody, sweet and infinitely complex with barnyard-to-honey facets. In India and the Middle East, oud is culture, luxury and spirituality combined. In perfumery it defines the pinnacle of oriental luxury. In Indian winters, oud unfolds for hours in magnificent complexity. In summer, the merest touch suffices. The undisputed king.
akigalawood: Akigalawood is a captive woody molecule smelling of patchouli, oud and spices with modern, radiant warmth. In perfumery it provides a contemporary woody-spicy signature. In India, its warm radiance suits evening wear. Modern woody innovation.
indian-oud: Indian oud, particularly from Assam's agarwood, is among the world's finest, deep, animalic and honeyed with distinctive character. Assam oud has ancient heritage. In perfumery, Indian origin marks top-tier oud. In Indian winters, Assam oud is the ultimate luxury, a heritage in scent form. The crown jewel of Indian perfumery.
cambodian-oud: Cambodian oud, or Krassna, smells honeyed, fruity and sweet with less barnyard than Indian varieties. It is the most approachable fine oud. In perfumery it offers a gentler entry to oud. In India, its honeyed sweetness is beloved. Oud with a smile.
patchouli-leaf: Patchouli leaf emphasises the natural, green-herbaceous aspect of patchouli before aging darkens it. In perfumery it offers a fresher patchouli experience. In India, its natural greenness suits those who find aged patchouli too heavy. Patchouli in its youth.
laotian-oud: Laotian oud smells woody, honeyed and refined with elegant depth. From Laos's forests, it offers a balanced oud experience. In perfumery it provides sophisticated oud character. In Indian winters, its refined depth is wonderful. Oud with Laotian grace.
palo-santo: Palo santo, or holy wood, smells sweet, woody and spiritually clear with distinctive minty-citrus facets over warm wood. Burned for cleansing in South America. In perfumery it brings a sacred, uplifting woodiness. In India, its spiritual character resonates. Holy wood's blessing.
java-vetiver-oil: Java vetiver oil is the Indonesian variety, smelling earthy and rich with distinctive depth. In perfumery it offers an alternative vetiver character. In India, its earthy richness connects with monsoon moods. Vetiver from the archipelago.
texas-cedar: Texas cedar, botanically a juniper, smells dry, warm and ruggedly American with a distinctive arid woodiness that evokes desert landscapes and frontier spirit. It is drier and warmer than other cedars, with a sun-baked character. In perfumery it brings a distinctive dry warmth to woody and aromatic compositions, particularly those with a Western or adventurous character. In India, Texas cedar's arid warmth offers an interesting contrast to tropical humidity, working well in dry heat and winter. It pairs beautifully with leather, tobacco and amber for a rugged oriental character. For those who like their woods with a touch of the wild frontier.
exotic-woods: Exotic woods is a blended impression of rare tropical hardwoods, all warmth, richness and faraway luxury. In perfumery it evokes distant forests and adventure. In India, exotic woods' warm richness suits winter. Adventure in timber form.
pine-needles: Pine needles capture the sharp, green, resinous scent of fresh needles, brighter than pine wood. In perfumery they bring vivid coniferous freshness. In India, pine needle scents evoke mountain air. In winter, their crisp brightness invigorates. Forest floor freshness.
hinoki-wood: Hinoki is Japanese cypress, smelling clean, lemony-woody and spiritually serene with temple-like calm. In perfumery it brings a meditative, refined woodiness. In India, hinoki's serene character offers peaceful contrast. Zen in wood form.
cedar-needles: Cedar needles offer the green, fresh aspect of cedar, brighter than the wood with aromatic vitality. In perfumery they add a fresh green-woody lift. In India, their fresh character suits pleasant weather. Cedar's green voice.
